oewn-04794222-n.learner: being free of anything that holds you back or makes you feel embarrassed.
examples: Perhaps he had been civil only because he felt himself at ease

oewn-04715389-n.learner: the state of having no difficulty, no hardship, and no effort.
examples: a person who can write a long letter with ease cannot write ill
now smiled at the rapidity and ease with which an affair was finally settled

oewn-14469215-n.learner: the state of being comfortable, or of feeling better after pain or trouble.
examples: Fixed there by the keenest of all anguish, self-reproach, she could find no interval of ease or forgetfulness.

oewn-00048072-r.learner: as well; on top of what has already been said.
examples: Miss Bingley saw all this likewise
The envelope itself was likewise full.
He rose to greet her, and his sister rose likewise.
Rich and poor were likewise welcome at the table.

oewn-01987278-v.learner: to get up onto your feet.
examples: When the gentlemen rose to go away
she saw Mr. Darcy rise also and follow him

oewn-01972576-v.learner: to go up to a higher place.
examples: when he ceased the colour rose into her cheeks
Smoke rose from the chimney into the still air.

oewn-00154951-v.learner: to grow greater in value, or to reach a higher point.
examples: Prices rose sharply after the poor harvest.

oewn-00458406-n.learner: the time when it is your part to do something, in an order people have agreed on.
examples: It will be her turn soon to be teased
Kitty simpered and smiled, and hoped her turn was coming soon.

oewn-00293443-n.learner: a short walk that goes out and comes back.
examples: let me persuade you to follow my example, and take a turn about the room

oewn-00350856-n.learner: the act of changing the direction you are going in, or of going back the other way.
examples: At the crossroads we made a turn to the right.

oewn-01839438-v.learner: to change where you are; to go, travel, or make your way, in a real or a figurative sense.
examples: Elizabeth at that instant moving towards them
he was moving that way; and fearful of its being Mr. Darcy, she was directly retreating

oewn-01854282-v.learner: to make something or someone shift into a new position or place, in a real or an abstract way.
examples: She is a great deal too ill to be moved.

oewn-02604860-v.learner: to live your life among a particular sort of people or surroundings.
examples: In a country neighbourhood you move in a very confined and unvarying society.

oewn-04920159-n.learner: a way of behaving that is polite and keeps to what people accept as good manners.
examples: the cold and ceremonious politeness of her courtesy and address
"Mr. Darcy is all politeness," said Elizabeth, smiling.

oewn-01230397-n.learner: the act of showing that you have regard for other people.
examples: Mrs. Bennet, all amazement, received her with the utmost politeness

oewn-04680827-n.learner: the habit of staying calm and seeming not to care; an easy lack of concern.
examples: He listened to her with perfect indifference
With an air of indifference, he soon afterwards added

connotation.why: casts a calm manner as not caring

oewn-04643967-n.learner: the habit of having no eagerness for and no interest in things in general.
examples: Years of illness had left him in a settled indifference to everything around him.

connotation.why: faults a person for taking interest in nothing

oewn-07498922-n.learner: a lack of interest that shows itself in no feelings being shown at all.
examples: She heard the news with complete indifference, and her face never changed.

oewn-01132241-n.learner: the pull of what people expect of you, which binds you to the actions it demands.
examples: which lead me to perform what I look on as a point of duty
"Neither duty, nor honour, nor gratitude," replied Elizabeth, "has any possible claim on me"

oewn-00720746-n.learner: work you have to do because right or the law requires it.
examples: You have now done your duty by her, and must fret no longer.
Had he done his duty in that respect, Lydia need not have been indebted to her uncle

oewn-13337021-n.learner: a tax the government charges on goods brought into or sent out of the country.
examples: The government raised the duty on imported wine.

oewn-00023953-n.learner: the feeling that stirs you to act towards something you want; the reason for the act, which gives your behaviour a purpose and a direction.
examples: The distance is nothing, when one has a motive; only three miles.
No motive can excuse the unjust and ungenerous part you acted there.

oewn-03794547-n.learner: a design or figure made of shapes or colours that come again and again, as on a building or in decoration.
examples: A leaf motive ran round the top of the wall.

oewn-07043169-n.learner: a tune or idea in a piece of music that comes back or is worked out further.
examples: The same motive returns in the last movement of the symphony.

oewn-02535833-v.learner: to make an effort to do something.
examples: "That it ought not to be attempted.
She attempted to speak, but no words came.

oewn-01654835-v.learner: to start on an activity or a piece of work.
examples: He attempted a translation of the whole poem.
